DC-2025-B260811.aiSummary: The bill would open and name several new streets in Square 1112-E in Ward 7, including 20th Street, 21st Street, Burke Street, 20th Place, 21st Place, C Place, and C Street. DC-2025-B260855.aiSummary: The measure would let the District create and run the Duke Business Improvement District, a local area where property owners pay extra fees for shared services. It sets the district’s boundary and lists the property types and tax rates that would apply, including rates for hotels, housing units, parking lots, and religious buildings. It also sets board membership rules and allows matching funds from the Greater U Street Parking Benefit Fund.

actions.text: Referred to Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0877 Introduced by Councilmember R. White at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260877.aiSummary: The measure would require the District’s corrections department to restore regular in-person contact visits at the Correctional Treatment Facility within 120 days and start a phased pilot for contact visits at the Central Detention Facility within 240 days. It would also set rules for when visits can be limited, require clear scheduling and visitor-approval steps, and call for family and disability accommodations. The bill would affect people held at those two facilities, their approved visitors, and the corrections department.

DC-2025-B260822.aiSummary: The bill would require the Mayor to hire an outside reviewer to study the District’s housing development costs and rules. The study would compare DC with nearby counties in Maryland and Virginia and measure things like total cost per unit, permit time, fees, taxes during construction, and other major delays. It would also point to rules that add cost or delay, say whether they are unique to DC or higher here than elsewhere, and recommend changes. The Mayor would then send the study to the Council within 30 days after it is finished.

DC-2025-B260819.aiSummary: The measure would require some condo associations to get reserve studies on repair and replacement costs and to update them every 5 years. It would also change how some inclusionary housing units are sold by giving the seller an equity payment on later resales, and it would change home purchase aid so lenders help with qualification while the Mayor makes the final call. It would create a local mortgage foreclosure prevention program and fund it with fees on home closings and foreclosure filings.

DC-2025-B260495.aiSummary: The bill would change condo insurance rules for unit owners in the District of Columbia. It would require certain unit owner policies to include at least $25,000 in dwelling coverage, $500,000 in liability coverage, and $25,000 in loss assessment coverage, and it would raise the most a unit owner may owe for a condo insurance deductible to $25,000 when damage starts in that unit. It would also let a condo association charge a unit owner for that deductible amount, and if a unit owner does not keep the required insurance, the association could buy a policy and bill the owner for the premium.

DC-2025-B260110.aiSummary: The bill would create a new Director of Recruitment and Retention in the Office of the City Administrator to find hard-to-fill jobs in District agencies and recommend ways to improve hiring and staff retention. It would let the Mayor offer up to $5,000 in recruitment incentives for new hires and retention payments for current workers in certain public safety and related jobs, and would require quarterly reports to the Council on hiring, departures, and money spent. It would also direct MPD, the Department of Corrections, and the Office of Unified Communications to run student outreach campaigns, and create an internship program at the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner for high school-age students.
